data_quality_assurance:
Yes, data quality assurance processes are foreseen to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the interview data. The following measures will be implemented:
Instrument Validation: The semi-structured interview guide provided by the consortium lead CSD will be cross-checked for question clarity and relevance among the consortium partners prior to data collection.
Data Capture Quality: Interviews will be audio-recorded to prevent data loss or distortion.
Transcription Standardisation: Audio files will be transcribed using a standardised protocol [e.g., verbatim / intelligent verbatim transcription].
Verification & Proofreading: All transcripts will be cross-checked and proofread against the original audio recordings by the researcher to correct any transcription anomalies or misinterpretations.
Anonymisation Checking: During the transcription review, all direct and indirect identifiers will be systematically removed or pseudonymized to maintain participant confidentiality while preserving context."

dmp.description:
SHIFT (Shaping Informed Frameworks for Trust) is an EU-funded Preparatory Action under call CNECT/2024/1917981 — European Narratives Observatory to fight Disinformation, coordinated by the Center for the Study of Democracy (CSD) and running from April 2026 for 18 months across 13 countries: 12 EU Member States and Moldova (BG, SK, CZ, MD, PL, DE, RO, DK, IE, LV, EE, LT, FR). The consortium brings together public policy research institutes, behavioural communication specialists, civic tech innovators, and NGOs: CSD, GLOBSEC, Alliance4Europe, CeMAS, Funky Citizens, Logiq Media, European Movement Ireland, Rīga Stradiņš University, and Make.org, with supporting engagement from the Thomson Reuters Foundation.
SHIFT builds the missing link in Europe's response to disinformation: going beyond detecting harmful narratives to testing what works to counter them. It combines cross-national research, audience segmentation, and real-world campaign testing to understand what works to counter disinformation and why.
SHIFT addresses a critical gap in Europe’s response to disinformation: moving beyond detection and debunking to understand what actually works to counter it. The project examines how harmful narratives shape beliefs, trust and behaviour across different audiences, with the aim of identifying effective, evidence-based strategies to mitigate their impact. SHIFT combines cross-national survey research, digital ecosystem analysis and behavioural audience segmentation to map how disinformation operates as a system of influence. It investigates how exposure to narratives affects public attitudes and identifies vulnerable and persuadable audience groups, providing a robust empirical foundation for targeted interventions. 
At its core, SHIFT introduces an “impact engineering” approach—applying data-driven experimentation to design, test and optimise counter-narratives in real-world conditions. Through multivariate campaign testing and iterative refinement, the project generates actionable evidence on what drives traction and behavioural impact, ultimately equipping policymakers, civil society and media actors with practical tools to strengthen responses to disinformation and FIMI at scale.
SHIFT pursues the following core objectives:
• Diagnose the impact of disinformation on beliefs, trust and behaviours across different societal groups, through harmonised cross-country research (surveys, focus groups, expert consultations, meta-narrative clustering and typologies) in all 13 countries.
• Map vulnerable audiences and narrative ecosystems by cross-national audience segmentation models based on behavioural, cognitive, and media consumption patterns, identifying persuadable population segments to inform targeted interventions.
• Design and pilot behavioural countermeasures and targeted communication strategies using A/B testing and iterative optimisation (40+ pilot interventions, 500,000+ individuals reached)
• Scale and translate findings into policy and practice: equip civic and policy actors with open-access toolkits, segmentation models and training to scale impact beyond the project
Structure
Phase I – Foundations (M1–6)
Development of a cross-national research framework, narrative typology and large-scale survey across 13 countries, including vignette-based experiments to assess susceptibility to disinformation.
Phase II – Action (M5–12)
Translation of research insights into audience-specific communication strategies, followed by multivariate A/B testing of narrative interventions in real digital environments.
Phase III – Scale & Impact (M10–18)
Evaluation and synthesis of results into an open-access narrative toolkit, cross-country analysis and policy recommendations, supported by stakeholder engagement and training.

Semi-structured interviews will be carried out with experts, RSU is responsible for conducting around 9 interviews in Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.
